title: Hypothermia
summary: Get them out of the cold, replace wet clothing, insulate them (including head and from the ground) and warm them gradually. Handle gently.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} for moderate or severe hypothermia
when: Confused, drowsy, slurred speech or clumsy
Shivering has stopped while still cold

steps.title: Get them out of the cold
steps.text: Move them into shelter, out of wind and rain. Handle them gently and keep them horizontal if severely cold.

steps.title: Replace wet clothing
steps.text: Remove wet clothing (cut it off if needed to avoid excessive movement) and replace with dry clothing.

steps.title: Insulate
steps.text: Wrap them in blankets, sleeping bags or a survival bag, covering the head and neck. Insulate them from the ground.

steps.title: Warm gradually
steps.text: Use warm (not hot) packs wrapped in cloth on the chest, armpits and neck if available. A warm room or vehicle helps.
points: If fully alert and able to swallow, give warm sweet drinks (not alcohol)

steps.title: Monitor
steps.text: Check breathing for up to a minute in a severely cold person – breathing may be very slow. If not breathing, start CPR.

doNot: Do not rub or massage limbs
Do not use hot baths, hot water bottles directly on skin or direct heat
Do not let a severely cold person walk or exert themselves

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
sources.title: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
International Consensus on CPR and ECC Science With Treatment Recommendations (CoSTR)

review.notes: Drafted from the cited guidelines. Must be checked by a qualified clinician against the current editions and local protocols before operational use.
